title: CatalystLoop vector refinement hosted API walkthrough

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/time: 2026-12-01 14:30 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (CatalystLoop), Luis Romero (CatalystLoop), Fiona Zhang (CatalystLoop)
Shared artifacts: relevance-playbook.pdf (link), benchmark-template.csv (link), console-tour.mov (link)

Auto-summary (auto): Brief demo of hosted embeddings + rerank endpoints, brief tour of Console and Optimize suggestions. Discussed security and pilot logistics.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll get started in a minute, appreciate the time, uh this is maya from redwood inference, with me is ethan our solutions engineer
[00:12] Ethan (Redwood): hey hi all, excited to walk through the embeddings + rerank flow and show the console bits that help you tune relevance
[00:20] Priya (CatalystLoop): thanks, yea we've been struggling with our FAQ search, too many false positives and the lexical fallback is noisy, so curious how your rerank pipeline looks
[00:32] Maya: perfect, that's exactly what this demo is geared toward. quick agenda: api for embeddings, hosted rerank endpoint, console metrics, and then optimize, which suggests batching/quantization and cache configs
[00:46] Luis: quick note — we run on GCP, and we currently use a custom FAISS index but open to replacing the service if latency and relevance improve. we also have strict data residency in eu-west-1 for customer logs
[01:01] Ethan: got it, we can pin model variants and region, and we support retention controls — you can opt out of storing logs or redact tokens; we also have customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest
[01:15] Priya: do you have SOC 2 and SSO support? we need SAML enterprise SSO and audit logs for compliance
[01:21] Maya: yes SOC 2 Type II, and SSO via SAML/Okta, and audit logs are available in the console or shipped to your SIEM. i'll share the security package after this call
[01:32] Ethan: jumping into the demo — here's the basic embed call, it's a simple POST /v1/embeddings with model param, payload with texts. response is a vector of floats. one thing to note: we have model profiles in the catalog labeled latency/cost/quality so you can pick the right tradeoff
[01:50] Maya: (screen) showing Console > API > Embeddings. you can see usage breakdown per token, per embedding, and sampling of vectors for QA
[02:05] Luis: how do you handle versioning? we need stable vectors across model upgrades for re-indexing costs
[02:12] Ethan: good q — you can pin to model version, and the console lets you create a migration plan. we also have quantization-friendly variants (8-bit/4-bit) to reduce storage and inference cost while preserving similarity in most workloads
[02:30] Fiona: when you say quantization-friendly, do you provide the quantized vectors or the model serving pathway? how does that work with our existing FAISS setup
[02:37] Ethan: we serve quantized model variants on the hosted side; for an external index you can either store full-precision vectors from our embeddings API or use reduced-dim/quantized vectors — we provide guidance on thresholds. for FAISS you might reindex but often 8-bit quant does well with reranking
[02:55] Priya: show me the rerank endpoint flow
[03:02] Maya: sure — it's a two-step pattern we recommend: retrieve top-k candidates from your vector store, then call /v1/rerank with query, candidates, and optional context. our reranker scores and returns a ranked list with explainability scores
[03:18] Ethan: (screen) demo: took a sample query 'how to reset password' — baseline recall from FAISS had false hits about account deletion, reranker re-ordered to surface the actual reset doc on top
[03:33] Luis: are the reranker models autoregressive or a cross-encoder? what's the latency like for 10 candidates
[03:40] Ethan: it's a cross-encoder style reranker optimized for low-latency; for 10 candidates typical p95 is ~60-90ms on our hosted profile, we've got profiles tuned for under 40ms if you sacrifice some precision
[03:55] Priya: that's promising, our SLO for end-user search is 200ms p95 so sounds doable
[04:02] Fiona: curious about cost — do you meter per candidate for rerank?
[04:07] Maya: rerank is metered per call and uses a per-candidate token estimate; we surface cost estimates in the Console and Predict tool — Optimize can suggest batching or caching to reduce unit cost
[04:20] Ethan: speaking of caching, we have prefix caching for conversational contexts and KV cache for model state. for search rerank we recommend local candidate caching and server-side TTL caching for frequent queries
[04:35] Priya: you mentioned Optimize earlier — show an example of a suggestion
[04:40] Ethan: yep — Optimize analyzed a sample workload and suggested increasing batch size to 8 for embeddings inference during off-peak, and flip the reranker to a lower-latency model at peak. it also suggested applying 8-bit quantization for storage which dropped cost by ~40% in a similar customer case
[04:58] Maya: (screen) here's Optimize -> Recommendations, with impact estimates and confidence score; you can apply suggestions or run a simulation in the console
[05:10] Luis: any automated fallback if the pinned model isn't available? we need graceful degradation for high availability
[05:15] Ethan: automatic fallback to a compatible variant in the same family, with configurable routing policies: latency-first, cost-first, or region-primary. can also do canary rollouts and automatic rollback on regression
[05:29] Priya: how do we prove quality doesn't regress during rollout? we run prompt sets and evals in CI
[05:34] Maya: we have per-prompt-set evals and quality monitoring — you can tie alerts to datasets so if your metric drops we notify and optionally rollback
[05:45] Fiona: for pilot, we want to run an A/B against our current FAISS+BM25 hybrid, what's the usual pilot footprint you recommend
[05:53] Ethan: 1-2 weeks with a 1% traffic shadow or a full-slice on a set of queries; we provide a benchmark harness and a Colab you can run. we'll also help pick metrics: MRR@10, NDCG, and latency percentiles
[06:09] Maya: i'm going to share the benchmark template and the console tour after this call — links are in the notes
[06:15] Priya: ok — switching gears — security: KMS, HSM integration? we have an internal HSM for key management
[06:22] Ethan: supported — you can bring your own KMS keys and we integrate with customer-managed keys for encryption at rest; for extreme cases we can discuss an on-prem/private deployment package with customer-controlled HSM
[06:35] Priya: and network isolation? we might prefer VPC peering or private endpoints
[06:40] Maya: we support private endpoints and VPC peering for enterprise; Dedicated and Private deployment modes give you more control — Dedicated for reserved capacity, Private for VPC/on-prem
[06:52] Luis: curious about throughput — we index millions of docs, peak embedding writes of 20k/day. how does batching help?
[06:59] Ethan: batching embeddings reduces per-vector overhead; Optimize can recommend batch sizes based on your sequence length distribution. e.g., batching to 32 payloads for small docs can cut per-embedding cost 2-3x in our numbers
[07:15] Fiona: if we do a pilot, who will be the primary contacts from redwood?
[07:19] Maya: me for project mgmt and commercial, ethan for technical setup and benchmarks. we'll loop in infra if you choose private networking
[07:28] Priya: timeline — we want a pilot before end of Q1, ideally run in Jan. can you support that?
[07:34] Maya: yes, pilot kickoff in early Jan is doable — we'll send the pilot template and the pricing; we can sign a short reserved capacity window if you want predictability
[07:45] Luis: small question — tokenization differences across models, if we switch models will embeddings drift a lot?
[07:52] Ethan: some drift happens, which is why we recommend pinning and a migration plan. Optimize can flag model-change regression anomalies during the rollout
[08:04] Priya: any places where transcription really breaks — sorry that was a random thought — ignore me
[08:07] Maya: (laughs) all good
[08:10] Ethan: showing a short live demo now — sending a batch of 16 docs to /v1/embeddings -> then FAISS retrieval -> /v1/rerank with top10 candidates. watch the console logs for latency and cost estimate
[09:00] [screen noise, demo plays]
[09:20] Priya: looks good, the rerank result highlights a confidence score — can we surface that in the UI for human review?
[09:26] Ethan: yes, the API returns score and optional explain tokens; Console can surface a flag when score < threshold for human-in-the-loop review
[09:40] Fiona: for the A/B do you generally suggest synchronous rerank vs async?
[09:46] Ethan: synchronous gives best UX but higher p95; async works for lower-priority queries. for search we usually do synchronous for top user-facing queries and async for batch background indexing
[09:58] Priya: are there rate limits we should be aware of for hosted?
[10:02] Maya: we have tenant-level quotas and can provision burst for pilots; we'll publish target SLOs in the pilot agreement
[10:12] Luis: any pitfalls with our faiss+bm25 hybrid we should watch out for during integration?
[10:17] Ethan: ensure your candidate set size is sufficient — too few candidates reduces rerank effectiveness; also canonicalize queries and docs to reduce surface noise. we'll share a checklist
[10:28] Priya: ok final question — do you manage embeddings lifecycle? like re-index triggers on model update
[10:34] Maya: we provide hooks and scripts for reindex; you can schedule rolling reindexes or do on-write updates. Optimize can also suggest incremental reindexing strategies
[10:45] Fiona: great, that covers most of it. let's recap next steps
[10:50] Maya: recap: we'll send pricing and pilot template (Maya), ethan sends benchmark harness (Ethan), catalystloop provides sample queries and stake holders (Luis/Fiona/Priya). schedule private networking deep dive if you choose private/dedicated
[11:07] Priya: sounds good — we'll target the dates discussed
[11:12] Maya: awesome thanks everyone, i'll follow up with links and the security pack. feel free to message me if any questions
[11:20] [call ends]

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "kv cache" transcribed as "K V cash"), product names shortened, and filler words retained to preserve meeting flow.
